world.title: French unions call nationwide strike as Macron faces election-year unrest
world.summary: French unions called a nationwide strike and demonstrations for Thursday, Nov. 5, bringing public- and private-sector workers together with students to protest living costs and conditions in public services and education. France’s domestic intelligence service forecast 500,000 to 700,000 demonstrators outside Paris, wh
world.content: French unions called a nationwide strike and demonstrations for Thursday, Nov. 5, bringing public- and private-sector workers together with students to protest living costs and conditions in public services and education. France’s domestic intelligence service forecast 500,000 to 700,000 demonstrators outside Paris, while the inter-union coalition expected 40,000 to 80,000 in the capital. Authorities planned to deploy about 70,000 police nationwide. Students have protested school conditions and prospects for young people for weeks, while unions have linked those concerns to wages and the cost of living. Riots and looting on Oct. 17 damaged shops and public buildings, prompting criticism of President Emmanuel Macron’s government’s response. The action is expected to disrupt rail services, schools and other public services. France’s next presidential election is five months away. Parliamentary talks over next year’s budget, which includes spending cuts, remain deadlocked.
world.image_alt: French unions call nationwide strike as Macron faces election-year unrest

world.title: Trump weighs Iran deal or renewed strikes after midterm defeat
world.summary: President Donald Trump’s administration is divided over whether to resume strikes on Iran, scale back military operations or seek a deal. The U.S. military is preparing for possible major combat as Qatari mediators work to prevent renewed fighting. Trump said the war contributed to Republican losses in the Nov. 3 midte
world.content: President Donald Trump’s administration is divided over whether to resume strikes on Iran, scale back military operations or seek a deal. The U.S. military is preparing for possible major combat as Qatari mediators work to prevent renewed fighting. Trump said the war contributed to Republican losses in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, citing higher fuel prices, but said he would make the same decision again and that Iran must not obtain a nuclear weapon. The conflict began with U.S.-Israeli strikes on Feb. 28 and spread as Iran attacked Gulf targets and shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The campaign damaged Iran’s military capabilities but did not resolve the nuclear issue; limited U.S. strikes on Iranian targets near the strait were reported on Nov. 2. Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has rejected expectations that the election will change U.S. policy and warned of a wider response to renewed attacks. Qatar is seeking U.S. and Iranian backing for a draft agreement that could avert renewed combat and restart direct talks in the coming days. Democrats take control of Congress in January 2027, when they are expected to investigate the administration and challenge its policies, though they cannot themselves compel an end to hostilities.
world.image_alt: Trump weighs Iran deal or renewed strikes after midterm defeat

world.title: Hackers alter controls at three French blood sites; no plasma lost
world.summary: France’s national blood service, the French Blood Establishment (EFS), said a cyberattack on refrigeration equipment at three of its sites on Nov. 2 raised temperature and defrost settings to extreme levels. The attack targeted a contractor’s systems rather than EFS directly. Monitoring alarms prompted staff to secure
world.content: France’s national blood service, the French Blood Establishment (EFS), said a cyberattack on refrigeration equipment at three of its sites on Nov. 2 raised temperature and defrost settings to extreme levels. The attack targeted a contractor’s systems rather than EFS directly. Monitoring alarms prompted staff to secure or move plasma and samples before they were damaged. EFS reported no loss of blood products, no identified health effects and no interruption to collections or distribution. The incident followed attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems in several European countries, after a separate wave hit hundreds of French stores in October and spoiled food. French authorities are investigating; remote access to the affected refrigerators has been disabled. Le Canard Enchaîné reported that attackers sought to raise settings from the usual minus 30 Celsius to 110 Celsius. The French Health Ministry and national cybersecurity agency are investigating, while the European Union said its agencies were discussing a coordinated response with national authorities. No group has claimed responsibility, and investigators have not established whether the refrigeration attacks are connected.
world.image_alt: Hackers alter controls at three French blood sites; no plasma lost

world.title: Pope Leo meets Bob Dylan, citing singer
world.summary: Pope Leo XIV met singer-songwriter Bob Dylan at the Vatican on Wednesday, Nov. 4, during Dylan’s Italian tour. During the brief private audience, the pope gave Dylan a rosary, and the musician gave Leo a copy of his autobiography, “Chronicles: Volume One”. Leo quoted Dylan’s 1963 protest song “Go Away You Bomb” in a bo
world.content: Pope Leo XIV met singer-songwriter Bob Dylan at the Vatican on Wednesday, Nov. 4, during Dylan’s Italian tour. During the brief private audience, the pope gave Dylan a rosary, and the musician gave Leo a copy of his autobiography, “Chronicles: Volume One”. Leo quoted Dylan’s 1963 protest song “Go Away You Bomb” in a book preface warning against rearmament and nuclear weapons. Dylan, 85, was in Rome ahead of a scheduled Thursday concert at the Palazzo dello Sport. Vatican officials said the encounter consisted of greetings and lighthearted exchanges; the Vatican press office did not immediately disclose what the two discussed. In 1997, Pope John Paul II quoted “Blowin’ in the Wind” while addressing young people at a gathering in Bologna where Dylan performed. Dylan’s Italian tour also includes Bologna, with further European dates scheduled later in November and December.
world.image_alt: Pope Leo meets Bob Dylan, citing singer

world.title: Zelensky honors Melania Trump for brokering Oleshky evacuation truce
world.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky awarded U.S. first lady Melania Trump the Order of Princess Olga, First Class, citing her humanitarian work and role in arranging a six-day ceasefire that enabled civilians to leave Russian-occupied Oleshky in the Kherson region. Zelensky signed the decree Nov. 2, and Ukraine publ
world.content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky awarded U.S. first lady Melania Trump the Order of Princess Olga, First Class, citing her humanitarian work and role in arranging a six-day ceasefire that enabled civilians to leave Russian-occupied Oleshky in the Kherson region. Zelensky signed the decree Nov. 2, and Ukraine published it Wednesday. The truce, which Ukrainian officials said Trump helped secure, was the longest local pause in fighting since Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion. Trump said nearly 800 people were evacuated. The pause allowed crews to clear mines from roads and residents to leave for Ukrainian- or Russian-controlled areas after weeks of food and medicine shortages. Trump is due to host Russian and Ukrainian representatives at the White House on Thursday, Nov. 5. Russian human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova and adviser Kirill Dmitriev are expected to meet Ukrainian ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets. Russia, Ukraine and the United States are also set to hold trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11, their first such meeting since February.
world.image_alt: Zelensky honors Melania Trump for brokering Oleshky evacuation truce

world.title: Bavarian deputy premier Hubert Aiwanger found dead in Berlin hotel
world.summary: Hubert Aiwanger, Bavaria’s deputy premier, economy minister and Free Voters party leader, was found dead in a Berlin hotel on Wednesday, Nov. 4. He was 55. Berlin police and prosecutors opened an investigation to establish the cause and circumstances of his death and rule out third-party involvement. Authorities have n
world.content: Hubert Aiwanger, Bavaria’s deputy premier, economy minister and Free Voters party leader, was found dead in a Berlin hotel on Wednesday, Nov. 4. He was 55. Berlin police and prosecutors opened an investigation to establish the cause and circumstances of his death and rule out third-party involvement. Authorities have not announced a cause. Aiwanger had traveled to Berlin for the opening of a Free Voters office but canceled his appearance after feeling unwell, according to German media reports. He was later found in his hotel room in the Mitte district. His death leaves a leadership vacancy in the Free Voters, the junior partner in Bavaria’s governing coalition with the Christian Social Union since 2018. Bavarian State Secretary Tobias Gotthardt is temporarily taking over Aiwanger’s government duties. The party’s succession arrangements remain unsettled; Aiwanger had planned to seek another term as federal party chairman the weekend after next.
world.image_alt: Bavarian deputy premier Hubert Aiwanger found dead in Berlin hotel

world.title: Mother and daughter found dead after suspected grizzly bear attack near Bella Coola
world.summary: A mother and daughter died in a suspected bear attack near Bella Coola, British Columbia, and officials are investigating whether more than one bear was involved. Jennifer “Jenny” Balcarras, 48, and Selah Reed, 20, were reported missing after what was expected to be a short walk. Searchers found Balcarras on Monday and
world.content: A mother and daughter died in a suspected bear attack near Bella Coola, British Columbia, and officials are investigating whether more than one bear was involved. Jennifer “Jenny” Balcarras, 48, and Selah Reed, 20, were reported missing after what was expected to be a short walk. Searchers found Balcarras on Monday and Reed on Tuesday in the Snooka West trail area. Investigators said evidence suggested an animal may have been involved, but the number of bears remains unclear. The British Columbia Conservation Officer Service and Royal Canadian Mounted Police are searching for and trying to trap any bears involved. Officers will assess captured animals and kill any bear they determine was responsible, citing public safety. Authorities have urged people to avoid the trail while the investigation continues. A grizzly attack on a school group in the Bella Coola area about a year earlier injured 11 people; that bear was never caught. The Nuxalk Nation established a recommended curfew for residents. Inspector Jeff Tyre of the British Columbia Conservation Officer Service said officers were in regular contact with the Nuxalk Nation and the Bella Coola community to provide updates. He said they were also in contact with the victims’ family to offer support.
world.image_alt: Mother and daughter found dead after suspected grizzly bear attack near Bella Coola

world.title: Hungary opens communist-era secret police files naming up to 60,000
world.summary: Hungary opened a searchable online database on Nov. 4 containing communist-era state security records linked to about 50,000 to 60,000 people. Prime Minister Péter Magyar led the release. The records include names and registration information; additional recruitment dossiers concerning about 9,000 people are due by Feb
world.content: Hungary opened a searchable online database on Nov. 4 containing communist-era state security records linked to about 50,000 to 60,000 people. Prime Minister Péter Magyar led the release. The records include names and registration information; additional recruitment dossiers concerning about 9,000 people are due by Feb. 25, 2027. The disclosure follows a September law granting broader public access after decades in which ordinary citizens generally could see only files about themselves or close relatives. Hungary’s state security services are estimated to have recruited about 150,000 informants during the communist period, but many records were lost or destroyed. A name in the database does not by itself prove that someone willingly informed on others: records can identify people who were monitored, pressured into recruitment or never submitted reports. Archivists warn that the files are incomplete. The government says it will withhold sensitive personal details and has arranged psychological support for people affected by the disclosures.
world.image_alt: Hungary opens communist-era secret police files naming up to 60,000

business.title: India backs four lithium and nickel plants with $297 million
business.summary: India’s Cabinet approved a 28.14 billion rupee ($297 million) subsidy program on Nov. 4 to establish four domestic processing plants—two for lithium and two for nickel—over five years, beginning in fiscal 2026-27. The government says the plan will reduce reliance on imported refined minerals and strengthen supply chain
business.content: India’s Cabinet approved a 28.14 billion rupee ($297 million) subsidy program on Nov. 4 to establish four domestic processing plants—two for lithium and two for nickel—over five years, beginning in fiscal 2026-27. The government says the plan will reduce reliance on imported refined minerals and strengthen supply chains for electric vehicles, batteries, electronics and defence. The plants would process ores and intermediate materials into high-purity compounds; cobalt could also be recovered during nickel processing. The government will screen companies for technical qualifications before they compete for subsidies, then select projects requesting the least government support. Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired the Cabinet meeting that approved the program.

business.title: U.S. private employers add 86,000 jobs in October, ADP says
business.summary: U.S. private employers added 86,000 jobs in October, matching September’s downwardly revised gain and exceeding economists’ forecasts of 69,000 to 75,000, according to payroll processor ADP. ADP’s figures can differ from the government’s more comprehensive payroll count. The U.S. Labor Department is scheduled to releas
business.content: U.S. private employers added 86,000 jobs in October, matching September’s downwardly revised gain and exceeding economists’ forecasts of 69,000 to 75,000, according to payroll processor ADP. ADP’s figures can differ from the government’s more comprehensive payroll count. The U.S. Labor Department is scheduled to release its October jobs report on Friday. Economists surveyed by Reuters forecast a 65,000 increase in total nonfarm payrolls and an unemployment rate of 4.2%; Fox Business also reported a 65,000 payroll-growth forecast.

business.title: California billionaire wealth tax trails as Proposition 42 advances
business.summary: California’s proposed one-time 5% tax on billionaires was trailing Wednesday, with about 55% of counted votes against it as the tally continued. Proposition 40 would tax the wealth of people who lived in California on Jan. 1, 2026, and had net worths above $1 billion. The Associated Press had not called the result, and
business.content: California’s proposed one-time 5% tax on billionaires was trailing Wednesday, with about 55% of counted votes against it as the tally continued. Proposition 40 would tax the wealth of people who lived in California on Jan. 1, 2026, and had net worths above $1 billion. The Associated Press had not called the result, and certification of the state’s final count could take weeks. The tax also faces two competing ballot proposals: Proposition 42 was ahead, while Proposition 41 was trailing. Either could block the tax if it receives more yes votes than Proposition 40, even if the wealth tax itself wins a majority. Supporters proposed using most of the revenue to help offset federal health funding cuts, while opponents warned that wealthy residents might leave, reducing California’s income-tax revenue.
business.image_alt: California billionaire wealth tax trails as Proposition 42 advances

business.title: Oil falls below $100 as US election raises Iran peace bets
business.summary: Oil prices dropped sharply on Nov. 4 after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress and Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for Republican losses. In Asian trading on Nov. 5, Brent crude was down 0.5% at $94.15 a barrel after falling 8.7% the previous day, while US benchmark West Texas Intermediate wa
business.content: Oil prices dropped sharply on Nov. 4 after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress and Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for Republican losses. In Asian trading on Nov. 5, Brent crude was down 0.5% at $94.15 a barrel after falling 8.7% the previous day, while US benchmark West Texas Intermediate was at $87.38. Traders interpreted the election result and comments from US and Iranian officials about diplomacy as signs that Washington could seek a settlement to a conflict that has disrupted global energy supplies for eight months. President Donald Trump has defended the war and left open further military action. The US carried out limited strikes on Iranian targets Monday and announced new sanctions on entities in India and Turkey on Wednesday. Analysts said a lasting price decline depends on a durable agreement; without one, high shipping costs and continued difficulty moving crude from the Gulf could push Brent back above $100.
business.image_alt: Oil falls below $100 as US election raises Iran peace bets

business.title: BMW warns car division could lose money as China sales fall
business.summary: BMW cut its forecast for its car division's 2026 operating margin to between -0.5% and 0.5%, warning that the business could post an operating loss after restructuring costs. The German automaker issued the warning on Nov. 3, a day before reporting that third-quarter net profit fell nearly 15% to €1.45 billion and reve
business.content: BMW cut its forecast for its car division's 2026 operating margin to between -0.5% and 0.5%, warning that the business could post an operating loss after restructuring costs. The German automaker issued the warning on Nov. 3, a day before reporting that third-quarter net profit fell nearly 15% to €1.45 billion and revenue fell 5.8% to about €30.5 billion. The company said its vehicle deliveries in China fell 24.8% in the quarter, while deliveries in Europe and the United States rose. BMW plans to cut up to 8,000 jobs in Germany by the end of 2027 and said severance costs and the faster introduction of newer models would weigh on results. Excluding restructuring charges, it expects the car division's 2026 margin to exceed 2%. BMW's Neue Klasse model range begins its China rollout this month with the iX3.
business.image_alt: BMW warns car division could lose money as China sales fall

business.title: Musk’s $474 million midterm push fails as Democrats take Congress
business.summary: Elon Musk spent about $474 million backing Republican candidates and political groups in the 2026 U.S. midterms, but Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress and defeated his preferred candidates in key races, including Texas Senate hopeful Ken Paxton. Musk’s companies rely on government contracts and are pla
business.content: Elon Musk spent about $474 million backing Republican candidates and political groups in the 2026 U.S. midterms, but Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress and defeated his preferred candidates in key races, including Texas Senate hopeful Ken Paxton. Musk’s companies rely on government contracts and are planning data-center expansion, particularly in Texas. Democratic lawmakers have said they want to investigate Musk’s government work and federal contracts. With control of congressional committees, they can use subpoenas to compel documents and testimony. Texas’ incoming Democratic governor, Gina Hinojosa, has proposed pausing new data-center construction until lawmakers set safeguards, including protections for household water and electricity costs. The new Congress takes office in January, when Democrats will lead committees overseeing federal spending and agencies that do business with Musk’s companies.
business.image_alt: Musk’s $474 million midterm push fails as Democrats take Congress

business.title: Bank of England expected to lift rate to 4% as inflation climbs
business.summary: The Bank of England is widely expected to raise its key interest rate from 3.75% to 4% on Thursday, Nov. 5, its first increase since August 2023, in response to higher inflation. Annual inflation reached 3.5% in September, above the Bank’s 2% target, with higher fuel and energy costs linked to the Iran war and supply d
business.content: The Bank of England is widely expected to raise its key interest rate from 3.75% to 4% on Thursday, Nov. 5, its first increase since August 2023, in response to higher inflation. Annual inflation reached 3.5% in September, above the Bank’s 2% target, with higher fuel and energy costs linked to the Iran war and supply disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. The Monetary Policy Committee’s decision is due at 12:00 GMT, alongside quarterly forecasts for inflation and economic growth. Higher rates would make borrowing more expensive and could increase returns on savings. Policymakers also face a weaker growth outlook and the risk that elevated energy costs will keep pushing prices up.
business.image_alt: Bank of England expected to lift rate to 4% as inflation climbs

business.title: CVS sets 2028 breakup, separating pharmacy chain from insurer and pharmacy-benefit manager
business.summary: CVS Health said Nov. 4 it plans to split into two publicly traded companies by the first half of 2028, separating its roughly 9,000-store pharmacy chain from its insurance and pharmacy-benefit businesses. The move partly reverses the U.S. healthcare company’s strategy of combining those operations: insurer Aetna, pharm
business.content: CVS Health said Nov. 4 it plans to split into two publicly traded companies by the first half of 2028, separating its roughly 9,000-store pharmacy chain from its insurance and pharmacy-benefit businesses. The move partly reverses the U.S. healthcare company’s strategy of combining those operations: insurer Aetna, pharmacy-benefit manager Caremark, CVS Specialty, Oak Street Health and Signify Health would remain under CVS Health, while CVS Pharmacy would include retail and mail-order pharmacies, MinuteClinic and Health100 technology services. Chief Executive David Joyner will lead CVS Health, and Prem Shah will lead CVS Pharmacy. Current shareholders are expected to receive shares in both companies. The announcement accompanied third-quarter results: revenue rose 5.4% to $108.4 billion, and adjusted earnings per share increased to $2.09 from $1.60 a year earlier. CVS also raised its 2026 earnings outlook. The company said the split follows a strategic review and will give each business more focus. Joyner said regulatory scrutiny was not driving the decision, though state and federal lawmakers have challenged the role of pharmacy-benefit managers. The separation is subject to required approvals and other conditions. CVS said both companies should retain investment-grade credit ratings. The split will not immediately change operations: CVS plans to continue serving customers during the transition and expects to complete the separation in the first half of 2028.
business.image_alt: CVS sets 2028 breakup, separating pharmacy chain from insurer and pharmacy-benefit manager

science.title: Neuroscientists propose brainstem source of feeling; separate study finds grid-like cortical activity
science.summary: Neuroscientists Marshall Devor and Mark Baron propose that the brainstem generates the basic feeling of conscious existence, while the cortex organizes more complex perceptions and thoughts. Their paper synthesizes clinical cases and earlier animal experiments rather than reporting a new experiment. They argue that pai
science.content: Neuroscientists Marshall Devor and Mark Baron propose that the brainstem generates the basic feeling of conscious existence, while the cortex organizes more complex perceptions and thoughts. Their paper synthesizes clinical cases and earlier animal experiments rather than reporting a new experiment. They argue that pain and consciousness can persist after extensive cortical damage, while small injuries to the upper brainstem can cause coma. Separately, a study using functional magnetic resonance imaging in 18 people found a sixfold, hexagonal activity pattern in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex as participants evaluated facial expressions and emotional phrases. The researchers say the pattern may help organize relationships among emotions, but the small study does not establish that it causes emotional processing.
science.image_alt: Neuroscientists propose brainstem source of feeling; separate study finds grid-like cortical activity

science.title: UN says developing countries need $305 billion a year for climate adaptation
science.summary: Developing countries will need about $305 billion a year by 2035 to adapt to climate change, nearly ten times the $28.2 billion to $31.7 billion in international public funding they received in 2024, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) said in its 2026 Adaptation Gap Report. Funding grew by about $1 billion
science.content: Developing countries will need about $305 billion a year by 2035 to adapt to climate change, nearly ten times the $28.2 billion to $31.7 billion in international public funding they received in 2024, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) said in its 2026 Adaptation Gap Report. Funding grew by about $1 billion from 2023. The report says the aspiration agreed at the COP30 climate talks to triple adaptation finance by 2035 would provide only $85 billion to $120 billion annually, covering 20% to 29% of estimated needs after inflation. The estimate largely excludes private-sector adaptation needs, which could nearly double the total. The report identifies institutional barriers and mounting climate-related losses as additional obstacles to carrying out adaptation plans. It was released ahead of COP31, scheduled to open in Antalya, Türkiye, on Nov. 9. Climate justice groups have identified adaptation finance as a priority for the talks, and UNEP Executive Director Inger Andersen urged countries to step up efforts to meet the COP30 tripling aspiration.
science.image_alt: UN says developing countries need $305 billion a year for climate adaptation

science.title: Sydney researchers observe hydrogen dissolved between metal atoms
science.summary: University of Sydney researchers have directly observed hydrogen dissolved in the spaces between metal atoms, rather than only at defects. The research, led by Professor Julie Cairney, was published in Nature. Hydrogen entering pipelines and storage equipment can cause cracking, a process known as hydrogen embrittlemen
science.content: University of Sydney researchers have directly observed hydrogen dissolved in the spaces between metal atoms, rather than only at defects. The research, led by Professor Julie Cairney, was published in Nature. Hydrogen entering pipelines and storage equipment can cause cracking, a process known as hydrogen embrittlement. The team used deuterium, a heavier hydrogen isotope, to trace hydrogen in metal alloys, combining atom-probe measurements with microscopy and calculations. First author Chao Huang said the next step is to test how hydrogen affects metal deformation and performance under stress, including in ultra-high-strength steels.
science.image_alt: Sydney researchers observe hydrogen dissolved between metal atoms

science.title: NASA unveils crewed X-70 test plane for advanced flight research
science.summary: NASA unveiled its crewed X-70 Fractal experimental aircraft at Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Wednesday as a platform for testing advanced flight controls and maneuverability. The agency says the plane’s controls can be rapidly reconfigured and it can carry experimental equipment inside or outside the aircraft. NAS
science.content: NASA unveiled its crewed X-70 Fractal experimental aircraft at Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Wednesday as a platform for testing advanced flight controls and maneuverability. The agency says the plane’s controls can be rapidly reconfigured and it can carry experimental equipment inside or outside the aircraft. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman expects its first flight for the agency within two years. The aircraft has a takeoff weight of 10,000 pounds, is designed to cruise at Mach 0.75 and reach 45,000 feet, and has an estimated range of 1,500 nautical miles. NASA has not named the aircraft’s builder or its first planned experiments. The concept image released with the announcement is labeled as generated content, not a confirmed depiction of the final aircraft.
science.image_alt: NASA unveils crewed X-70 test plane for advanced flight research

science.title: Archaeologist argues Iron Age ruler Verica was a woman
science.summary: Bournemouth University archaeologist Miles Russell argues that Verica, an Iron Age ruler of the Atrebates in southern Britain, was a woman, challenging the long-standing view that Verica was male. Russell points to Verica’s name, coin imagery he interprets as a bare-breasted female rider, and inscriptions that could me
science.content: Bournemouth University archaeologist Miles Russell argues that Verica, an Iron Age ruler of the Atrebates in southern Britain, was a woman, challenging the long-standing view that Verica was male. Russell points to Verica’s name, coin imagery he interprets as a bare-breasted female rider, and inscriptions that could mean “daughter of” rather than “son of.” Verica was exiled around 40 CE and sought help from Emperor Claudius; the Roman historian Cassius Dio linked that appeal to Rome’s invasion of Britain in 43 CE. The interpretation is disputed. Oxford archaeologist Roger Tomlin said Russell needs examples showing that Rome used the title “rex” for both male and female rulers, while coin specialist Daphne Nash Briggs noted that some Verica coins appear to show male figures. Russell presented his argument in a discussion published in Current Archaeology and also develops it in his book on the British ruler Caratacus.
science.image_alt: Archaeologist argues Iron Age ruler Verica was a woman

science.title: JWST image-processing method boosts exoplanet sensitivity up to 15-fold
science.summary: Astronomers have developed a physics-based method to remove residual starlight from James Webb Space Telescope images, improving sensitivity to faint planets by two to 15 times and revealing the known giant exoplanet 51 Eridani b at a wavelength where earlier processing failed. The method, called Physics-based Learning
science.content: Astronomers have developed a physics-based method to remove residual starlight from James Webb Space Telescope images, improving sensitivity to faint planets by two to 15 times and revealing the known giant exoplanet 51 Eridani b at a wavelength where earlier processing failed. The method, called Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets, or FLIP, models the telescope’s optics and adjusts for small changes that make conventional reference-star images imperfect matches. The method works with existing observations without changes to telescope hardware. The team is now reprocessing the hundreds of coronagraphic images JWST has collected to look for additional planets. Researchers say the approach could ease strict stability requirements for future observatories, but further work is needed to reduce computing costs and test it on larger data sets.
science.image_alt: JWST image-processing method boosts exoplanet sensitivity up to 15-fold

science.title: Very strong El Niño drives floods and drought risks worldwide
science.summary: A very strong El Niño is driving sharply different weather hazards: record rain and flooding have hit Florida and the U.S. Four Corners, while the Philippines faces worsening dry spells and drought risk. Two feet of rain fell in Florida’s Malabar area in 36 hours on Nov. 1-2; Philippine forecasters expect below-normal
science.content: A very strong El Niño is driving sharply different weather hazards: record rain and flooding have hit Florida and the U.S. Four Corners, while the Philippines faces worsening dry spells and drought risk. Two feet of rain fell in Florida’s Malabar area in 36 hours on Nov. 1-2; Philippine forecasters expect below-normal rainfall across much of the country. The climate pattern is strengthening unusually warm Pacific waters and shifting atmospheric circulation. Climate scientist Daniel Swain of the University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources said climate change is adding to El Niño’s effects. The World Meteorological Organization forecasts a December peak and expects the event to persist into February 2027. Philippine projections warn of drought in 87 provinces by March, while the U.S. forecast points to continued wet conditions in the South and a flood threat shifting toward California.
science.image_alt: Very strong El Niño drives floods and drought risks worldwide

science.title: Ancient DNA links Germanic and Celtic languages to migrations
science.summary: Two studies combining ancient DNA with archaeological and linguistic evidence traced migrations that may have spread Germanic and Celtic languages across Europe. Researchers analyzed DNA from more than 4,500 ancient people, including 712 newly sequenced genomes. A previously unidentified migration into Scandinavia from
science.content: Two studies combining ancient DNA with archaeological and linguistic evidence traced migrations that may have spread Germanic and Celtic languages across Europe. Researchers analyzed DNA from more than 4,500 ancient people, including 712 newly sequenced genomes. A previously unidentified migration into Scandinavia from around the Baltic Sea about 4,000 years ago may have brought an early form of Germanic, later than the arrival roughly 5,000 years ago proposed in earlier accounts. A second migration, westward from central Europe around 3,000 years ago, may help explain the spread of Celtic languages. The findings challenge the theory that Celtic originated on Europe’s Atlantic coast. The studies also identified migration from northern Germany into Denmark and southern Sweden about 1,500 years ago, coinciding with the emergence of Old Norse and contributing to the ancestry of later Vikings. The researchers cautioned that DNA cannot establish which language an individual spoke. The studies were published in Nature on Nov. 4, 2026.
science.image_alt: Ancient DNA links Germanic and Celtic languages to migrations

sports.title: Fernandes backs Carrick as United assess manager after Roma fightback
sports.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes said he accepts head coach Michael Carrick’s decision to bench him and rejected claims of a rift, as the club weighs its next move after Tuesday’s 3-2 comeback win over Roma ended a nine-game winless run. Fernandes said the players were focused on improving together, not saving
sports.content: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes said he accepts head coach Michael Carrick’s decision to bench him and rejected claims of a rift, as the club weighs its next move after Tuesday’s 3-2 comeback win over Roma ended a nine-game winless run. Fernandes said the players were focused on improving together, not saving their head coach’s job, and that reports about their relationship contained “a lot of lies”. Carrick cautioned against getting carried away by the victory. The club had already planned to keep him through Sunday’s Premier League match against Aston Villa and reassess his position during the international break. The comeback eased the immediate pressure but did not change those plans. Academy winger Shea Lacey, 19, came on for the final 15 minutes and set up Matheus Cunha’s winner, prompting Carrick to praise his attacking skill and defensive work. United next host Villa on Sunday, while Cunha’s dismissal means he will miss the Champions League visit to Sporting on November 25.

sports.content: Aston Villa and head coach Unai Emery have committed to continuing together beyond 2029, with talks on a new contract described as advanced and an agreement close. Emery met chairman Nassef Sawiris and senior football executives on Wednesday to discuss the club’s long-term plans, while Villa said Emery would continue to lead the club’s sporting project. Emery has been linked with Manchester United as a possible replacement for manager Michael Carrick, whose position remains uncertain despite Tuesday’s 3-2 comeback win over Roma, which ended a nine-game winless run. United face Villa on Sunday before the international break and would need to pursue alternatives to Emery if they replace Carrick.

sports.content: The Baltimore Ravens are finalizing a trade to acquire Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett. The deal is expected to be completed this weekend, with compensation still undisclosed. Starter Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury requiring surgery, while backup Tyler Huntley suffered a season-ending toe injury. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano is set to start Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Brissett cannot join the Ravens in time for Thursday’s game; he is expected to make his Baltimore debut against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16. The Ravens are 4-4 and have lost three straight games, scoring no more than 13 points in each.

sports.title: McIlroy calls for men’s golf reset after LIV’s collapse
sports.summary: Rory McIlroy, the world No. 2 golfer, said men’s professional golf needs a reset after LIV Golf’s spending and player recruitment intensified competition with established tours. Speaking before the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship on Nov. 4, he backed DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings’ statement that LIV represent
sports.content: Rory McIlroy, the world No. 2 golfer, said men’s professional golf needs a reset after LIV Golf’s spending and player recruitment intensified competition with established tours. Speaking before the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship on Nov. 4, he backed DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings’ statement that LIV representatives had spoken of wanting to “destroy” the European-based circuit. Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund withdrew its backing after investing more than $5 billion in LIV since its 2022 launch. LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September. A proposed relaunch with BC Partners financing remains uncertain as leading players depart. McIlroy argued that sustainable business practices matter more than an arms race in prize money. Kinnings said returning players must earn their place under the DP World Tour’s 2027 membership and invitation rules. Jon Rahm, who has left LIV, plans to play the DP World Tour in 2027, while his route back to the PGA Tour remains unresolved.

sports.content: Detroit Lions All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell said Wednesday he has full movement in his lower body and is making progress moving his upper body after suffering a neck injury in Sunday’s 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings. Campbell remains hospitalized. He said he is optimistic but gave no timetable for recovery or a return to football. Campbell was hurt while tackling Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter at Detroit’s Ford Field on Nov. 1. He lay motionless as medical staff treated him, secured him to a backboard and took him to the hospital. He was alert and breathing during the transfer. Players from both teams gathered around him, and play stopped for about 10 minutes. The Lions said Monday that preliminary indications were positive but provided no further details. Lions coach Dan Campbell said the team must acknowledge the emotional impact while preparing for Sunday’s road game against the Miami Dolphins. The Lions have added linebacker K.J. Britt to their active roster, signed Joe Bachie from the practice squad and added Owen Pappoe to the practice squad as they adjust to Jack Campbell’s absence.

sports.content: West Ham United’s new head coach Scott Parker began his second spell at the club with a 3-3 draw at Cardiff City on Wednesday, November 4, after his side recovered from a three-goal halftime deficit. West Ham appointed the former midfielder on a two-and-a-half-year deal after dismissing Nuno Espírito Santo; the Championship club had slipped to eighth after 13 matches and were six points behind leaders Middlesbrough. Parker met the players for the first time at 9 a.m. on matchday. Cardiff striker Jack Moylan scored all three of the hosts’ first-half goals, but Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman scored after the break to earn West Ham a point. Parker said he changed the team’s tactics and urged them to press more aggressively; he called the second-half response the night’s biggest positive. Parker led Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley to promotion from the Championship, but his teams were relegated from the Premier League in each of his full seasons there. He said he had achieved promotion in all three of his Championship campaigns.

sports.title: LIV Golf loses rescue deal worth up to $300 million, faces liquidation
sports.summary: BC Partners Credit has withdrawn its proposed investment of up to $300 million to relaunch Saudi-backed LIV Golf, leaving the breakaway men’s circuit facing a possible wind-down and asset liquidation. The firm pulled out after LIV failed to secure enough player commitments for its planned 2027 season, as prominent golf
sports.content: BC Partners Credit has withdrawn its proposed investment of up to $300 million to relaunch Saudi-backed LIV Golf, leaving the breakaway men’s circuit facing a possible wind-down and asset liquidation. The firm pulled out after LIV failed to secure enough player commitments for its planned 2027 season, as prominent golfers departed or declined to commit. The rescue plan, branded LIV 2.0, was meant to replace funding from Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, which said in April it would stop financing the league after 2026. LIV filed for bankruptcy protection in September. LIV had been pursuing a player-led ownership model, but the European circuit, the DP World Tour, decided to bar LIV 2.0 players from its 2027 membership, making it harder for golfers to commit while keeping options open elsewhere. LIV is due to appear at a bankruptcy court hearing in Trenton, New Jersey, on Thursday, Nov. 5. The hearing is expected to address contracts, leases and assets, but it is unclear whether the court will decide the league’s ultimate fate. South Australia’s premier said he does not expect LIV’s scheduled Adelaide tournament in March 2027 to go ahead.

sports.content: Arsenal beat Slavia Prague 2-1 in the Champions League on Wednesday, November 4, with Viktor Gyökeres setting up Noni Madueke’s ninth-minute opener before scoring in the 38th minute. The win left manager Mikel Arteta’s side third in the league phase with 10 points from four matches and extended their unbeaten start in the competition. Gyökeres, making his sixth start of the season, scored his second goal in three outings after going scoreless in his first 10 appearances for Arsenal. Slavia, who had managed one first-half shot, attacked more forcefully after the break. Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya made key saves and Gabriel Magalhães cleared off the line before Wiktor Nowak scored in the 90th minute. Slavia registered 17 second-half shots, but Arsenal held on. Arteta said Arsenal’s second-half control fell below his expectations, while Raya identified turnovers and Slavia’s higher press as problems to address. Arsenal return to league action against Hull City on November 7, then host Borussia Dortmund in Europe on November 24.
